A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SageAttention2 and provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting a reliable comparison. Both end with references; neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original kernel benchmarks, quantization ablations and end-to-end model evaluations, including Table 11.

after.justification: V2 reports original accuracy and speed experiments, including model-quality comparisons in Tables 10–11 and generation latencies in Table 12.

M1.justification: V2 replaces per-warp quantization with materially different per-thread token grouping and introduces an FP32 buffer for accumulating FP22 block products. Adaptive layer/timestep precision selection is removed. V smoothing becomes optional and is explicitly excluded from the main experiments, matching the revised Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both retain the same text benchmarks, needle-in-a-haystack task, Open-Sora video prompts, MJHQ-30K image prompts and ImageNet variants. The evaluated model roster changes, but no distinct dataset, task requirement or represented population is introduced.

E2.justification: V2 adds the original SageAttention to the end-to-end comparisons in Tables 10–11, although it already participated in v1's kernel benchmarks. TIMM comparisons also add HadmdAttn and SmoothAttn; v1 compared TIMM only against full precision. These substantially expand the evaluated controls.

E3.justification: V2 adds CogvideoX 1.5-5B, HunyuanVideo, Mochi and Stable-Diffusion3.5 model configurations while removing Open-Sora as an evaluated model. Kernel testing drops head dimension 256 on both GPUs. Table 12 adds generation-latency comparisons and Llama3.1 first-token measurements at 48K and 100K tokens; datasets and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V1's layer/timestep error analysis and adaptive-precision ratio study, Figures 7 and 15, are removed. Granularity comparisons are revised for per-thread quantization, and v2 adds HunyuanVideo cases and revises CogvideoX examples. The V-smoothing ablation is retained unchanged as Table 13 rather than newly added.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 7 reports means and standard deviations across inputs for layer/timestep accuracy. V2 removes this variability reporting with the adaptive analysis and provides no replacement uncertainty estimates or newly specified repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: V2 replaces mixed-precision result rows with separate revised 4-bit and 8-bit results, expands model results and changes retained entries; for example, Flux's full-precision FID changes from 11.303 to 10.960. New Table 12 reports CogvideoX 1.5-5B latency of 1040 seconds originally versus 577 seconds with SageAttn-8b. These are revised or newly reported results, not controlled v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 corrects the signs in the online-softmax rescaling recurrences. V2 Equations 5–6 replace warp-level scaling rules with explicit thread-group index and scale definitions. These are localized mathematical revisions; neither version supplies a theorem-and-proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion replace the advertised per-warp, Q/V-smoothing and adaptive-precision contributions with per-thread quantization, Q smoothing and FP32 buffering. The broad plug-and-play applicability and approximately threefold/fivefold speedup claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 removes the interpretation of persistent layer/timestep errors motivating adaptive precision and explains how FP32 buffering confines accumulation errors to individual tiles. Section 3.6 newly qualifies V smoothing as offering marginal benefits unless V has channel-wise biases, noting their absence in Llama3.1 and excluding smoothing from the main experiments.

D1.justification: V2 supplies the mma.m16n8k64 token-to-thread mapping, scale indexing and explicit FP22/FP32 buffer operations. V1's model-specific adaptive-precision ratios disappear with that procedure. CUDA, Ubuntu 22.04, RTX4090/L20 hardware and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for NVIDIA PTX documentation, HunyuanVideo, Mochi and Stable-Diffusion3.5, and clarifies FlashAttention3's Hopper-specific applicability. The broader positioning relative to linear/sparse attention, SageAttention, Qserve and QuaRot is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and approach summary are revised, smoothing and quantization subsections are reordered, and Smooth V is relabeled optional. The overall section hierarchy and much background, evaluation and explanatory prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 expands Figure 1 with video examples, redraws the workflow, adds the per-thread mapping diagram and revises qualitative comparison panels. Adaptive-analysis and head-dimension-256 plots disappear. The end-to-end table expands across Tables 10–11, and a generation-latency table is added, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 adds predecessor-baseline comparisons and application-latency measurements in Tables 10–12, while Sections 3.3–3.4 make hardware mapping and accumulation more explicit. These improve practical validation and reproducibility. The gain is limited by dropped head-dimension-256 tests and the absence of an isolated ablation validating the newly central FP32 buffer.
